source.title: Proposed Experiment to Test Local Hidden-Variable Theories
Experimental consequences of objective local theories
Hidden Variables, Joint Probability, and the Bell Inequalities

exceptions.description: One Distribution is shared by all four settings pairs, so a model in which the hidden variable knows the settings is outside this candidate. The freedom-of-choice loophole and superdeterminism are therefore not refuted by any gate built on these claims.

A response function takes only its own party's setting, so a model in which one outcome depends on the distant setting is outside this candidate. What makes that restriction physical is the spacelike separation assumed by the evidence record, not anything proved here.

Distribution carries a Finset support with real weights, so the claims cover finite mixtures of deterministic strategies. Extending them to a general probability measure on a continuous hidden-variable space is not done here.
Both bounds are stated for two parties with two settings each, matching the experiment. Chained or multipartite inequalities are outside the candidate.

title: Local realism: deterministic local response functions over a shared hidden variable
